questions.question: Evaluate: (-9) - (-60) ÷ (-15) + (-4) × 9
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Evaluate: (-9) - (-60) ÷ (-15) + (-4) × 9

**Formula used:**

Follow BODMAS (Bracket, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

**Calculation:**

⇒ (-9) - [(-60) ÷ (-15)] + [(-4) × 9]

⇒ (-9) - 4 + (-36)

⇒ -9 - 4 - 36

⇒ -49

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: The average weight of Mohan, Mohammad and Ashish is 45 kg. If the average weight of Mohan and Mohammad be 43 kg and that of Mohammad and Ashish be 46 kg, then the weight of Mohammad (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of Mohammad = (Total weight of Mohan & Mohammad) + (Total weight of Mohammad & Ashish) − (Total weight of all three)

⇒ Mohammad's weight = (2 × 43) + (2 × 46) − (3 × 45)

⇒ Mohammad's weight = 86 + 92 − 135

⇒ Mohammad's weight = 178 − 135 = 43 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 43 kg.**

questions.question: The radius of a right circular cone is 3.5 cm and slant height is 0.21 m, then what is the lateral surface area? (Use pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert units to standard forms: r = 3.5 cm, and l = 0.21 m = 21 cm.

Use the direct formula for Lateral Surface Area = π × r × l

Area = (22/7) × 3.5 × 21 = 11 × 21 = 231 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 231 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

• 
 
 l = 21 cm
 r = 3.5 cm
 
 
 

**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 3.5 cm

Slant height of the cone (l) = 0.21 m

**Formula Used:**

Lateral Surface Area of a right circular cone = πrl

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, convert slant height into centimeters: l = 0.21 × 100 = 21 cm

⇒ Substitute the values into the lateral surface area formula.

⇒ L.S.A. = (22/7) × 3.5 × 21

⇒ L.S.A. = 22 × 0.5 × 21

⇒ L.S.A. = 11 × 21

⇒ L.S.A. = 231 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 231 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

It is the total sum of the lateral surface area and the circular base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the capacity enclosed inside the conical surface: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height, radius, and perpendicular height form a right triangle which follows Pythagoras theorem: l = √(r² + h²).

When expenditure is constant, reduction % in consumption = [R / (100 + R)] × 100

Given R = 22.5%

Reduction % = (22.5 / 122.5) × 100 = (9 / 49) × 100

questions.question: Amit invests a sum of ₹5400 and Gopal invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Gopal gets ₹600 more interest than Amit, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in Simple Interest for 5 years = ₹600

Simple Interest on the difference for 1 year = ₹600 ÷ 5 = ₹120

Rate % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Difference in Principal) × 100

Rate % = (120 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 3%

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Amit: ₹5400
 
 
 Gopal: ₹9400

 

 

 

 
 
 Difference: ₹4000
 Extra SI = ₹600

 SI on ₹4000 for 5 years = ₹600

**Given:**

Principal for Amit (P₁) = ₹5400

Principal for Gopal (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 5 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹600

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI of Gopal − SI of Amit = ₹600

⇒ [(P₂ × R × T) ÷ 100] − [(P₁ × R × T) ÷ 100] = 600

⇒ [(P₂ − P₁) × R × T] ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ [(9400 − 5400) × R × 5] ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ (4000 × R × 5) ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ 20000R ÷ 100 = 600

⇒ 200R = 600

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 200

⇒ R = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. The interest earned remains constant for every year if the rate and principal are unchanged. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the interest rate and time period are the same, the difference in interest earned on two distinct principal amounts is exactly equal to the simple interest calculated on the difference between those principals.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike Simple Interest, Compound Interest is calculated on the initial principal as well as the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: Amount = P × (1 + R/100)T.

questions.question: Shan has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Piyush and Manoj and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Piyush and Manoj got same amount after 18 and 19 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Shan give to Manoj?

Ratio of Piyush's share to Manoj's share = (1 + 10/100)¹⁹ − ¹⁸ = 11/10.

Total parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts.

Manoj's share = (10 / 21) × 1218 = ₹580.

questions.question: A man sold an article for ₹216, there by gaining 12.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:

Fractional value of 12.5% = 1 ÷ 8

Let Cost Price (CP) = 8 units, then Profit = 1 unit.

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = 8 + 1 = 9 units.

9 units = ₹216 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹216 ÷ 9 = ₹24.

Cost Price (CP) = 8 units = 8 × 24 = ₹192.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Selling Price (SP) of the article = ₹216

Gain (Profit) Percentage = 12.5%

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 CP = ?
 
 
 SP = ₹216
 
 

 + 12.5% Profit
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP + 12.5% of CP = ₹216

**Calculation:**

⇒ 216 = CP × (100 + 12.5) ÷ 100

⇒ 216 = CP × 112.5 ÷ 100

⇒ 216 = CP × 9 ÷ 8

Loss Percentage

questions.question: Govind invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Govind got ₹280.5 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of Simple Interest for 2 years at 4% = 4% + 4% = 8%

Effective rate of Compound Interest for 2 years at 4% = 4% + 4% + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%

Given Compound Interest (8.16%) = ₹280.5

Simple Interest (8%) = (280.5 × 8) ÷ 8.16 = ₹275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹280.5

**Formula Used:**

Direct relation between CI and SI for 2 years: CI = SI × (1 + R/200)

 
 Principal (P)
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Year 1: ₹137.5
 
 
 Year 2: ₹137.5
 
 
• 
 4% on Interest
 
 
 Extra: ₹5.5
 
 Total CI = ₹280.5 | Total SI = ₹275

**Calculations:**

⇒ CI = SI × (1 + 4/200)

⇒ 280.5 = SI × (1 + 1/50)

⇒ 280.5 = SI × (51/50)

⇒ SI = (280.5 × 50) ÷ 51

⇒ SI = 14025 ÷ 51

⇒ SI = 275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain principal can be directly calculated by the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)².

Effective Rate Method

For a given rate R% per annum, the effective compound interest rate for 2 years is (2R + R²/100)%, whereas the simple interest rate is exactly 2R%. Comparing these effective rates is the fastest way to switch between CI and SI values.

Rule of 72

A mathematical shortcut used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed compound interest rate: Years ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is ₹3,500. If the selling price is ₹2,800, then the discount percent is:

 ₹700

**Calculations:**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed or tagged on an article. All percentage discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Successive Discounts

When two individual discounts d₁% and d₂% are given one after another, the net equivalent discount percent is given by: (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

This is the percentage by which a shopkeeper prices an item above its Cost Price (CP) to set the Marked Price. Formula: Mark-up % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: 400 pears were bought at ₹1250 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹900. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of pears.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP of 400 pears = 4 × 1250 = ₹5000

Total SP of 400 pears = 5000 + 900 = ₹5900

SP of 1 pear = 5900 ÷ 400 = 59/4

SP of 1 dozen (12 pears) = (59/4) × 12 = 59 × 3 = 177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of pears bought = 400

Rate of purchase = ₹1250 per 100 pears

Total profit earned = ₹900

**Formula Used:**

Total SP = Total CP + Profit

SP per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total Quantity) × 12

 
 Total CP

 (for 400 pears)

 ₹5900
 (for 400 pears)
 
 
• 
 

 + Profit ₹900
 
 
 SP per dozen = ₹177

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP for 400 pears = (400 ÷ 100) × 1250

⇒ Total CP = 4 × 1250 = ₹5000

⇒ Total SP = Total CP + Profit

⇒ Total SP = 5000 + 900 = ₹5900

Profit & Loss Percentage

Unitary Method for Pricing

To find the cost of a specific quantity (like a dozen), calculate the cost of a single unit first: Price of 1 Unit = Total Price ÷ Total Quantity.

Marked Price & Discount

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 16 : 23. If the difference between the numbers is 224, what is the smaller number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in ratio parts = 23 − 16 = 7 parts

7 parts = 224 ⇒ 1 part = 32

Smaller number = 16 parts = 16 × 32 = 512

**∴ The correct answer is 512.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of the two numbers = 16 : 23

The difference between the two numbers = 224

 
 16 parts (Smaller)
 Num 1
 
 
 23 parts (Larger)
 Num 2
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 

 

 Diff: 7 parts = 224

 1 part = 32 → 16 parts = 512

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 16x and 23x respectively.

⇒ Difference between the numbers = 23x − 16x

⇒ 7x = 224

⇒ x = 224 ÷ 7

⇒ x = 32

⇒ The smaller number = 16x

⇒ 16 × 32 = 512

**∴ The correct answer is 512.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportion Rule

When two ratios are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), the product of the extremes is always equal to the product of the means: a × d = b × c.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two different ratios a : b and c : d is calculated by multiplying the respective terms together to form ac : bd.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a basic ratio a : b is defined as the ratio of their squares, which is written as a² : b².

questions.question: x varies inversely to the square of y. Given that y = 5 when x = 6, find the value of x when y = 4.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For inverse square variation, the product of the first variable and the square of the second variable remains constant.

x₁ × y₁² = x₂ × y₂²

6 × 5² = x × 4²

150 = 16 × x

x = 150 ÷ 16 = 9.375

**∴ The correct answer is 9.375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x varies inversely to the square of y.

Initial values: x = 6 when y = 5

New condition: Find x when y = 4

**Formula Used:**

x ∝ 1 ÷ y² ⇒ x = k ÷ y² (where k is the constant of proportionality)

 
 Case 1
 x₁ = 6
 y₁ = 5
 
 Case 2
 x₂ = ?
 y₂ = 4
 

 

 
 x₁ × y₁² = x₂ × y₂²
 Inverse Square Variation

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the value of constant k using Case 1:

⇒ 6 = k ÷ 5²

⇒ 6 = k ÷ 25

⇒ k = 6 × 25 = 150

⇒ Now, substitute k and the value of y for Case 2 to find x:

⇒ x = 150 ÷ 4²

⇒ x = 150 ÷ 16

⇒ x = 75 ÷ 8 = 9.375

**∴ The correct answer is 9.375.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When one variable increases proportionally with another, they are in direct variation. Formula: x ∝ y ⇒ x ÷ y = k.

Inverse Variation

When one variable increases while the other decreases proportionally, they are in inverse variation. Formula: x ∝ 1 ÷ y ⇒ x × y = k.

Joint Variation

When a variable depends directly or inversely on the product of two or more other variables. Example: x ∝ y × z ⇒ x = k × y × z.

questions.question: X can do a job in 20 days, Y in 30 days and Z in 36 days. Y and Z begin the work but have to leave after 5 days. How many complete number of days will X take to finish the remaining job?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 30, 36) = 180 units

Efficiency: X = 9, Y = 6, Z = 5

Work done by Y and Z in 5 days = (6 + 5) × 5 = 55 units

Remaining work = 180 − 55 = 125 units

Days taken by X = 125 ÷ 9 = 13.88 ≈ 14 days

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by X = 20 days

Time taken by Y = 30 days

Time taken by Z = 36 days

Y and Z start the work and leave after 5 days.

**Method Used:**

We will use the LCM method to find the total work and the individual efficiencies.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 X
 20
 180
 9
 
 

 Y
 30
 6
 
 

 Z
 36
 5
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = LCM(20, 30, 36) = 180 units.

⇒ Efficiency of Y and Z working together = 6 + 5 = 11 units/day.

⇒ Work done by Y and Z in 5 days = 11 × 5 = 55 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 180 − 55 = 125 units.

⇒ Time taken by X to complete the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of X

⇒ Time taken by X = 125 ÷ 9 = 13.88 days.

⇒ Since 13 whole days will only cover 117 units of work, X will need an additional part of the 14th day to finish the remaining 8 units.

⇒ Thus, the number of complete days needed to fully finish the job is 14 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Approach

Total work is generally considered as the LCM of the time taken by each individual. Efficiency is then calculated as Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept works on the identical principle of Time & Work. The only variation is that an outlet pipe or a leak performs negative work as it empties the tank.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual amount of work done by each person. If everyone works for the same number of days, the wages can be distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 370 m and 330 m are running at speeds of 90 km/h and 150 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = 370 + 330 = 700 m

Relative speed (same direction) = 150 − 90 = 60 km/h

Speed in m/min = (60 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 1000 m/min

Time taken = Distance ÷ Speed = 700 ÷ 1000 = 0.7 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.7 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 370 m

Length of faster train (L₂) = 330 m

Speed of slower train (S₁) = 90 km/h

Speed of faster train (S₂) = 150 km/h

 
 
•

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₂ − S₁

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5 ÷ 18)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 370 + 330 = 700 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 150 − 90 = 60 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 60 × (5 ÷ 18) = 50 ÷ 3 m/s

⇒ Time taken in seconds = 700 ÷ (50 ÷ 3)

⇒ Time taken = (700 × 3) ÷ 50 = 42 seconds

⇒ Convert seconds to minutes = 42 ÷ 60

⇒ Time taken = 0.7 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.7 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = |S₁ − S₂|.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing Objects with Length

When a train crosses another train, a platform, or a bridge, the total distance covered is equal to the sum of the lengths of the train and the object.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5 ÷ 18). To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).
</p

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 20%, 35% and 20% in three successive months, but increases by 50% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original price of the fuel be 100.

Applying the multiplying fraction method for successive changes: −20% → 4/5 | −35% → 13/20 | +50% → 3/2

Final Price = 100 × (4/5) × (13/20) × (4/5) × (3/2)

Final Price = 100 × (624 ÷ 1000) = 62.4

Overall percentage change = 100 − 62.4 = 37.6% decrease

**∴ The correct answer is 37.6% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price decreases successively by 20%, 35%, and 20%, then increases by 50% in the fourth month.

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 − R₁/100) × (1 − R₂/100) ... × (1 + Rₙ/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of fuel be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (1 − 0.20) = 80

⇒ Price after 2nd month = 80 × (1 − 0.35) = 80 × 0.65 = 52

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 52 × (1 − 0.20) = 52 × 0.80 = 41.6

⇒ Price after 4th month = 41.6 × (1 + 0.50) = 41.6 × 1.50 = 62.4

⇒ Total decrease = Original Price − Final Price = 100 − 62.4 = 37.6

⇒ Percentage decrease = (37.6 ÷ 100) × 100 = 37.6%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.6% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity changes by a% and then successively by b%, the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100. Always use positive signs for increase and negative signs for decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

To quickly calculate multiple percentage changes, convert each percentage change into a fraction multiplier (e.g., −20% = 80/100 = 4/5) and multiply them consecutively with the initial base value.

Equal Successive Increase and Decrease

If any base value is first increased by x% and then decreased by the exact same x%, the final outcome is always a net decrease equal to (x² ÷ 100)%.
</p

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 2340 and 1551 to leave 40 and 33 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the greatest dividing number, subtract the remainders from the given numbers and find their HCF.

Required Number = HCF of (2340 − 40) and (1551 − 33)

⇒ HCF of 2300 and 1518

⇒ HCF of (23 × 100) and (23 × 66)

⇒ 23 × 2 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dividends = 2340 and 1551

Remainders = 40 and 33

**Formula Used:**

Greatest number = HCF of (Dividend₁ − Remainder₁) and (Dividend₂ − Remainder₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First exact divisible number = 2340 − 40 = 2300

⇒ Second exact divisible number = 1551 − 33 = 1518

⇒ Prime factorization of 2300 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 23 = 2² × 5² × 23

⇒ Prime factorization of 1518 = 2 × 3 × 11 × 23

⇒ The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the product of the lowest powers of all common prime factors.

⇒ Common factors are 2 and 23.

⇒ HCF = 2¹ × 23¹ = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest Dividing Number leaving Same Remainder

If a number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, the required number is the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Relation Between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers A and B, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the numbers themselves. Formula: HCF × LCM = A × B.

Least Number Leaving Same Remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves remainder r in each case is: LCM of (x, y, z) + r.
</p
